name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,277

clue.text: Giving seat, I moved to the end counter?

indicators.note: The clue tells you to take the I and shift it to the end of the seat word, a rearrangement of its letters.

blocks.clueFragment: seat, I moved to the end
blocks.note: A seat is a CHAIR; move its I to the end to get CHARI.
A counter is a flat surface, like a TABLE.

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their chair and wanders off to the end of a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'counter' is used loosely: a table is a flat surface you work at, much like a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means generous, inclined to give.

clue.text: Refuge close to church and leafy glade

indicators.note: The close of 'church' is its last letter.

blocks.note: The last letter of 'church'.
An arbour is a shady bower of trees or climbing plants.

explanation.surface: A peaceful retreat near a church, set in a leafy glade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to church' reads as 'near a church'; here it means the final letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: literally a sheltered anchorage for ships, and figuratively any place of safety.

clue.text: Make a mess of text checking someone’s home?

blocks.note: In text-message shorthand, 'are you' is written R U.
Someone at home is IN.

explanation.surface: Someone sends a text asking whether a friend is home, and somehow messes it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The text that checks whether someone is home reads 'R U IN?', which is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to spoil a plan or a meal completely.

clue.text: Vegetable providing clue for PI

blocks.note: The command word a setter could write to tell you to flip letters round.
PI written backwards: the letters such a command would act on.

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint about a vegetable, written in the style of a crossword setter's note.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as a command plus two letters, and solving that little clue gives PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is one of many root vegetables.

clue.text: Escape damage from crossbow?

blocks.note: Escape here is a noun: a hideaway you run to when you need to get away.
A crossbow fires short arrows called bolts, which punch through what they hit.

explanation.surface: Somebody dodges injury from a crossbow shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second, whimsical reading: a hole left by a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Escape' is used as a noun for a hideaway; the second sense is a literal hole left by a crossbow bolt.

clue.text: Dog avoiding black bird

indicators.note: The dog word steers clear of the letter for black, so B is dropped.

blocks.note: A beagle is a breed of dog.
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils.

explanation.surface: A dog keeps away from a black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' looks like one phrase; 'black' belongs to the wordplay and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one large bird of prey among the many kinds of bird.

clue.text: The cop’s leg fidgets — it could stop trousers falling off?

definitions.text: it could stop trousers falling off?

indicators.note: Something that fidgets won't keep still, so the letters move about.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A police officer's leg is twitching, and something is needed to keep his trousers up.
explanation.walkthrough: The trousers are not being worn: they are hanging on a washing line, where a peg stops them falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg clips washing to a line so it cannot fall.

clue.text: On reflection, treasure, I’d rather cuddles later

indicators.note: The phrase wraps its arms around the answer, holding it inside.
A reflection shows things back to front, so the hidden letters read right to left.

blocks.note: The letters REIDRAT span 'treasuRE, I'D RATher'.

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it over and tells their darling they'd rather cuddle later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuddles' seems to be something the treasure is doing; it actually says the phrase holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardier means more late, that is, later.

clue.text: Tip: try hard to change, providing limited coverage

indicators.note: The letters are told to change their order.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A piece of advice: try hard to change, even if it only goes so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' is insurance: a third-party policy covers only damage to others, not to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-party insurance is the minimum, limited level of cover.

clue.text: Legitimate to return age 50, having left before

indicators.note: Returning goes back the way it came, so the age word is read backwards.
The letter for left is placed in front of the rest.

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left.
Taken as written.
L is the Roman numeral for 50.

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is lawful to go back to being fifty, having already moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having left' reads as departing; it is the letter L, set before the reversed AGE and 50.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something legitimate is permitted by law.

clue.text: Metal coating for incinerator working

indicators.note: A coating is on the outside, so only the outer letters of 'incinerator' are taken.

blocks.note: The first and last letters of 'incinerator'.
A machine that is working is ON.

explanation.surface: A metal lining is needed for an incinerator that is in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal coating' looks like one phrase; 'Metal' is the definition and 'coating' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the commonest metals, the main ingredient of steel.

clue.text: Healthy concealing flings? Most dodgy

indicators.note: The healthy word hides the flings word inside itself.

blocks.note: To be healthy is to be FIT.
To shy is to fling or throw, as at a coconut shy.

explanation.surface: Someone who looks healthy is hiding their affairs, which is the most suspicious thing of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flings' suggests romances; here it is the verb, as in throwing a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy means suspicious or dodgy, so fishiest is most dodgy.

clue.text: Armies scattered, dividing north and south — close call

indicators.note: Scattered troops are thrown out of order, like these letters.
The rearranged letters come between N and S, splitting them apart.

blocks.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north.
The letters to rearrange.
S is the compass abbreviation for south.

explanation.surface: Scattered armies split a country into north and south, and disaster was only just avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North and south' sound like regions of a country; they are just the compass letters N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is something that almost happened, a close call.

clue.text: Shot took out sheltering king

indicators.note: The 'took out' word shelters the king inside it.

blocks.note: To take someone out romantically is to date them.
R is short for rex, Latin for king.

explanation.surface: A gunman fired, then killed a king who was hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'took out' read as violence; 'Shot' means moved fast, and 'took out' means went on a date with.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot across a room is to dart; shot and darted both mean moved swiftly.

clue.text: Suddenly drop breathing apparatus during exercise

indicators.note: The breathing organ comes during, that is inside, the exercise letters.

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise.
A lung is the body's breathing organ.

explanation.surface: A diver abruptly lets go of their breathing gear mid-workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing apparatus' suggests scuba gear; it is the body's own lung.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: prices or divers do this when they fall sharply.

clue.text: Impotent celebrity

definitions.note: Read as the two words NOT ABLE.

blocks.note: Impotent means powerless, unable; split the answer into two words for this sense.
A celebrity is a person of note, a famous figure.

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ABLE for the first sense; kept whole it is a noun for a well-known person.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the answer means lacking power; whole, it is a noun for a person of note.

clue.text: Medical centre initially called lab investigating new index cases

indicators.note: Take the words' initial letters.

blocks.clueFragment: called lab investigating new index cases
blocks.note: The first letters of the six words.

explanation.surface: A health centre phoned the lab to look into newly identified patient-zero cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Index cases' is epidemiology for the first known infections, which makes the surface convincing medical jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a place, often for outpatients, where medical treatment or advice is given.

clue.text: Despite expectations, rate fall is staggering

indicators.note: Staggering is lurching unsteadily, so the letters lurch out of order.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: An economics headline: contrary to forecasts, the interest rate drop is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' reads as 'astonishing'; it means reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: After all means in spite of what was expected.

clue.text: Child, advanced learner, missing nothing

blocks.note: A tot is a small child.
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced.
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate.

explanation.surface: A gifted child learning quickly without skipping a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing nothing' reads as part of the child's description; it is the definition, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: a total eclipse or failure is complete, with no part left out.

clue.text: Finish second work — about time!

indicators.note: The work goes about, around, the time letter.

blocks.note: S is short for second.
OP is short for opus, a work.
T is short for time.

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone finally finishing a second piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as impatience; it means OP wraps round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to stop work is to bring it to an end.

clue.text: Falsely sue a son of Isaac

indicators.note: Done falsely, the letters are put wrongly.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: Someone brings a false lawsuit against one of Isaac's sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a verb of the surface story; with the 'a' it supplies the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau is the elder twin son of Isaac, brother of Jacob.

clue.text: All voices express disapproval over it

indicators.note: Turned over, the word flips back to front.

blocks.note: Tut is the sound of disapproval.
Taken as written.

explanation.surface: A whole choir voices its disapproval of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All voices' seems to be the choir doing the disapproving; it is the definition, a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for 'all', marks a passage for every voice or instrument together.

clue.text: Horse feeding device began so peculiarly

indicators.note: Arranged peculiarly, the letters come out in an odd order.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A horse's feeder started working in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Began so' reads as part of the story; it is the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a bag of feed hung over a horse's muzzle.

clue.text: Behaves contrarily, surrounded by mean people and no-hopers

indicators.note: Going contrarily means going the opposite way, so the letters run backwards.
The reversed word sits inside the word for mean people.

blocks.note: To behave is to act.
A louse is a contemptible person; louses is its plural in that sense.

explanation.surface: Someone behaves awkwardly among nasty people and failures.
explanation.walkthrough: In the sense of a nasty person, louse takes the plural louses, not lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a hopeless case, a no-hoper.
